response.enhanced_information: Octreotide is the drug of choice for acute bleeding esophageal varices, acting as a somatostatin analogue to effectively reduce portal venous pressure and control hemorrhage. It is supported by evidence of its physiological interactions and its direct role in managing variceal bleeding. Propranolol serves more as a preventive measure, while ethanolamine oleate and phytonadione have specific uses that do not primarily address the immediate control of acute variceal bleeding.
